evals.name: selected-queue-to-workspaces
evals.prompt: I ran workstream-reconcile and selected wterm and emulate. Set up Herdr so I can resume both, using their local checkouts and the handoffs in my notes vault.
evals.expected_output: The skill proposes one workspace per selected checkout, keeps implementation cwd in each repo, treats the vault as optional read-only context, asks approval before mutation, and leaves unselected workstreams untouched.
assertions: Creates or reuses one workspace per exact checkout rather than one workspace for the vault
Uses the notes vault as context without making it the implementation cwd
Presents the topology plan before creating or moving Herdr resources
Does not materialize unselected queue items

evals.name: minimal-persistent-topology
evals.prompt: Prepare my repo in Herdr with Codex as the main agent and a persistent dev server. Also keep Fable and Grok open forever in adjacent panes in case I need review.
evals.expected_output: The skill keeps only the lead and verified runtime process persistent, explains that reviewers are launched on demand, and does not start a dev command until it is discovered and requested.
assertions: Keeps at most lead and runtime as persistent panes
Does not create standing reviewer agents
Discovers the repository-native dev command instead of assuming one
Does not install dependencies during topology setup

evals.name: visible-solution-gate-specialists
evals.prompt: Solution Gate needs two independent shaping passes. Make them visible in Herdr using Cursor Fable and Grok, wait for both, and give the artifacts back to the gate.
evals.expected_output: The skill launches two uniquely named, read-only, on-demand agents in the repo workspace after resolving current model IDs, monitors bounded lifecycle states, and returns evidence handles without deciding the gate.
assertions: Keeps Solution Gate as the method owner
Resolves model IDs from the installed runtime before launch
Uses unique visible Herdr agent names and read-only runtime modes
Does not count timeout, unknown, blocked, stalled, or empty output as evidence

evals.name: idempotent-resume
evals.prompt: Set up agent-browser in Herdr again. I think there is already a workspace with that name, but I do not remember which checkout it points to.
evals.expected_output: The skill inspects the existing workspace and pane cwd, reuses only an exact checkout match, and proposes rather than silently repairing a collision or moving user panes.
assertions: Does not reuse a workspace from its label alone
Checks the absolute checkout behind existing panes
Avoids duplicate workspaces when identity matches
Requires approval before moving or closing existing panes

evals.name: near-miss-prioritization
evals.prompt: Look through all my handoffs and decide which three projects I should work on this week. Do not set up any terminals yet.
evals.expected_output: The request routes to workstream-reconcile or another prioritization method, remains read-only, and does not invoke Herdr topology setup.
assertions: Does not claim ownership of portfolio prioritization
Routes stale handoff reconciliation to workstream-reconcile
Does not create workspaces, tabs, panes, or agents

evals.name: outside-herdr-fallback
evals.prompt: Run Solution Gate from a normal terminal where HERDR_ENV is unset. Herdr is installed elsewhere on the machine.
evals.expected_output: The owning gate uses its normal Agent surface without attaching to or controlling another Herdr session, and reports Herdr visibility as unavailable rather than blocking the method.
assertions: Does not inspect or control Herdr when HERDR_ENV is unset
Falls back to the owning skill's Agent surface
Does not block Solution Gate solely because Herdr visibility is unavailable

evals.name: control-cockpit-boundary
evals.prompt: Keep one master Herdr session open from my preferred notes vault so I can monitor wterm and emulate. Put every coding agent and dev server inside that master workspace too.
evals.expected_output: The skill proposes one optional single-pane control workspace rooted at the configured context location, keeps implementation and runtimes in repo-scoped workspaces, and uses Herdr's global state and sidebar instead of duplicating project panes.
assertions: Keeps the control workspace to one coordinator pane
Does not host implementation workers or dev servers in the control workspace
Treats the control root as configurable context rather than a required vault
Uses custom workspace, tab, pane, and globally unique agent labels
Uses event-driven blocked or done reporting instead of a standing reviewer panel
